memory_update.text: Add MU as the most direct US-listed HBM supplier exposure for the AI accelerators and HBM memory node; prioritize HBM revenue, capacity sold-through, qualification status, and customer concentration in Layer 2.
Add AMAT and LRCX as HBM capacity-enabling wafer-fab/advanced-packaging equipment vendors; their relevance depends on incremental HBM process-step intensity and memory WFE order conversion.
Add KLAC and CAMT as yield-control and inspection/metrology plays for advanced packaging and HBM; CAMT is smaller but has unusually direct HBM/AI inspection order evidence.

For this node, the investable chokepoint map should separate direct HBM suppliers, HBM process-tool suppliers, advanced-packaging capacity, inspection/metrology yield tools, substrates/interposers, and accelerator customers.

Next pass should verify US-listed exposure to HBM substrates, interposers, thermal interface materials, test handlers/probers, EDA/IP for HBM PHY/controller integration, and OSAT/advanced-packaging providers with ADRs or US listings.

summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the HBM/AI-accelerator chokepoint into memory supply, wafer-fab equipment, advanced-packaging tools, inspection/metrology, and process-control yield nodes. The highest-relevance additions for this pass are MU, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, and CAMT; all appear to clear the USD 1B market-cap preference based on current market data, but this is not a recommendation and requires deeper evidence checks on revenue exposure, customer concentration, and cycle risk.
